source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 171: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 1 - Attribute redundancy to KV-cache-driven turn economics: the agent re-calls because nothing in its context marks the prior result as authoritative.
Mechanism. A redundant calculator call is emitted when the decoder's next-token distribution over the tool-call sentinel exceeds the distribution over a direct answer. Nothing in the serialized context distinguishes 'a tool already returned 42' from 'a number appeared in text'. If the tool result is rendered as plain assistant text rather than a typed tool-result message with an id, the model has no structural feature to condition abstention on.
Falsifiable hypothesis H1. Rendering prior tool results as typed, id-bearing tool-result messages (native chat-template role, not inlined prose) reduces the unnecessary-call rate (UCR) by a relative >=25% with no drop in final-answer exact match beyond 1 absolute point.
Metrics. (a) UCR = redundant_calls / total_calls, where redundant is defined by an offline oracle: the identical normalized expression already appears in a prior tool-result in the same trajectory. (b) tool_success_rate. (c) final_answer_correctness (exact match + numeric tolerance). (d) trajectory_length in turns and in decoded tokens. (e) p50/p95 tool latency. (f) recovery_rate after a deliberately injected tool error.
Controlled experiment. Fixed eval set, N>=500 trajectories, single seed set, same weights. Arm A: current prose rendering. Arm B: typed tool-result rendering. Everything else frozen. Paired per-item comparison, McNemar on correctness, bootstrap CI on UCR.
Confounders. Template change also shifts tokenization, so trajectory_length changes are not attributable to behavior alone; control by reporting UCR per-call, not per-token. Prompt-length change alters cache-hit rate on the serving side and can move latency independently of model behavior.
Numbers. No MEASURED values are available here. Any 25% figure above is an ESTIMATE stated as the pre-registered decision threshold, not an observed result; it is derived from choosing an effect size larger than the run-to-run UCR noise typically seen when only decoding seeds change.
Rollback. Revert the template change if final-answer correctness drops >1 absolute point, or if p95 end-to-end latency regresses >10% on the serving canary.
Scope. This is a scaffold/serialization claim about the system. It is not evidence of any model domain capability.
risks: Typed-message change is a chat-template change and can silently break loss masking if reused in training
UCR oracle based on string-normalized expression matching will misclassify semantically identical but textually different queries
Latency deltas may be caused by prefix-cache behavior, not by fewer calls
evidence_required: Trajectory logs with typed tool-result boundaries and call ids
Per-item paired correctness table for arms A and B
Serving-side p50/p95 latency and prefix-cache hit rate for both arms

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 173: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 2 - Treat the abstention decision as a threshold on a calibrated self-consistency signal, and test whether calibration transfers off-distribution.
Mechanism. Sample k=5 short direct answers at T=0.7 before any tool call. If the normalized answers agree at rate >=tau, answer directly; otherwise call the tool. This turns 'should I call' into an explicit, tunable operating point rather than an emergent behavior.
Falsifiable hypothesis H2. A self-consistency gate with tau tuned on a dev split holds its operating point on a held-out split drawn from a different scenario family: UCR reduction on held-out is within 20% relative of the dev-split reduction. If the gate only works in-domain, H2 is false and the gate must not be shipped as a global default.
Metrics. UCR, false-abstention rate (answered directly but wrong when the tool would have been right), tool_success_rate, final correctness, added decode cost in tokens for the k samples, p95 latency.
Controlled experiment. Three arms: A baseline, B gate at tau, C tool-always. Sweep tau over a grid, produce a UCR-vs-false-abstention ROC. Pre-register tau before touching the held-out split.
Boundary conditions. The gate costs k extra short generations per query, so it is only defensible where tool latency exceeds the added decode latency. Under high batch pressure the extra samples compete for the same GPU and can raise queue delay for all tenants.
Confounders. Self-consistency agreement correlates with question difficulty, so UCR falls partly because easy items dominate the eval set; report UCR stratified by difficulty bucket.
Numbers. tau, k=5 and the 20% transfer band are ESTIMATEs chosen as pre-registration values, not measurements. The cost claim 'k extra generations' is a structural consequence of the design, not a benchmark result.
Rollback. Disable the gate if false-abstention rate exceeds baseline error by >0.5 absolute points, or if p95 latency under production concurrency regresses >10%.
Scope. Provisional system-level design. No claim about model domain competence.
risks: Extra sampling multiplies decode cost and can regress tail latency under concurrency
Threshold tuned on one scenario family may not transfer, producing confident wrong answers
Difficulty imbalance in the eval set can manufacture an apparent UCR win
evidence_required: Dev and held-out UCR/false-abstention curves with the pre-registered tau marked
Stratified UCR by difficulty bucket
Concurrency sweep showing p95 latency with and without the gate

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 174: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 3 - Contrarian on metrics: 'unnecessary call' is not directly observable, so ship a counterfactual-based estimator or report nothing.
Problem. Every naive UCR definition smuggles in an unverifiable assumption about what the agent 'already knew'. Grepping for a prior identical result measures textual repetition, not knowledge.
Mechanism of a defensible estimator. For each observed call, replay the trajectory with the call suppressed and force a direct answer. The call is unnecessary iff the counterfactual answer is correct. This is expensive but it is the only definition that is falsifiable per item.
Falsifiable hypothesis H3. The cheap textual-repetition proxy and the counterfactual estimator agree on >=80% of calls. If agreement is below that, all previously reported UCR numbers must be labeled invalid and re-derived.
Metrics. counterfactual-UCR (primary), proxy-UCR (secondary), per-item agreement matrix, cost of replay in GPU-seconds.
Controlled experiment. Sample 300 calls stratified by scenario family. Run both estimators. Report Cohen's kappa, not just raw agreement.
Boundary conditions. Replay is only valid if the tool is deterministic and side-effect free; a calculator qualifies, a retrieval or a stateful API does not. Do not extend this estimator to side-effecting tools.
Numbers. The 80% and N=300 are ESTIMATEs used as pre-registered thresholds. 300 is chosen so a proportion near 0.8 has a binomial 95% half-width of roughly 5 points, which is the resolution needed to accept or reject an 80% bar; that arithmetic is stated so a reviewer can check it.
Rollback. If replay cost exceeds the eval budget, do not fall back silently to the proxy; publish the proxy with an explicit validity warning instead.
Scope. This is an evaluation-methodology claim. It produces no capability claim of any kind.
risks: Counterfactual replay is invalid for stateful or side-effecting tools
Replay cost may exceed the evaluation GPU budget and tempt a silent fallback to the proxy
Low kappa retroactively invalidates prior reported numbers, which is a reporting hazard
evidence_required: Per-call agreement matrix and Cohen's kappa between proxy and counterfactual estimators
GPU-seconds consumed by the replay run
Explicit list of tools certified deterministic and side-effect free

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 175: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 4 - Intervene with a deterministic pre-tool cache keyed on the normalized expression; keep the model untouched.
Mechanism. Insert a middleware layer between the agent and the calculator. Normalize the expression (whitespace, operator ordering where commutative, numeric literal canonicalization), hash it, and serve from an in-process LRU on hit. The model still emits the redundant call; the fleet stops paying for it.
Falsifiable hypothesis H4. Cache hit rate on redundant calls exceeds 70% and end-to-end p95 latency improves, with byte-identical final answers versus baseline on the full eval set.
Metrics. cache hit rate, byte-identical-answer rate versus baseline, p50/p95 latency, calls-per-trajectory reaching the real tool, correctness unchanged.
Controlled experiment. Shadow mode first: compute what the cache would have returned and compare to the real tool output on every call, without serving from cache. Only enable serving after a shadow window with zero mismatches.
Boundary conditions. Normalization is where correctness dies. Floating-point associativity means reordering operands is not always safe; restrict normalization to whitespace and exact literal forms unless a mismatch-free shadow window proves more. Cache must be scoped per tenant if any expression could be sensitive.
Numbers. 70% is an ESTIMATE serving as the go/no-go bar, not a measurement. It is set above 50% so the layer clearly beats a coin-flip-quality win and justifies the added component.
Rollback. Any shadow mismatch, or any post-enable answer divergence, disables the cache immediately via a config flag with no redeploy.
Scope. Purely a serving-system optimization. It changes cost and latency and says nothing about the model's reasoning or domain knowledge; the redundant behavior still exists in the weights.
risks: Aggressive expression normalization can change numeric results under floating-point non-associativity
Cross-tenant cache sharing can leak query content
Masking the defect in serving removes pressure to fix the underlying behavior
evidence_required: Shadow-mode mismatch log covering the full comparison window
Cache hit rate broken down by redundant vs first-time calls
Byte-diff of final answers between cached and uncached arms

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 176: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 5 - Distributed-systems framing: quantify the redundancy tax on the shared cluster before authorizing any training run.
Mechanism. Redundant calls consume decode turns; each extra turn re-enters the scheduler, occupies KV-cache blocks, and lengthens the running batch. On a shared multi-tenant cluster the externality lands on unrelated tenants as queue delay, not on the agent's own latency.
Falsifiable hypothesis H5. Eliminating redundant calls yields a measurable reduction in aggregate KV-cache block-seconds and in p95 queueing delay for co-resident tenants under fixed offered load. If block-seconds do not move, the redundancy is not the bottleneck and no training intervention is justified on cost grounds.
Metrics. KV-cache block-seconds per trajectory, running-batch occupancy, scheduler queue delay p95, GPU utilization, tokens decoded per trajectory, and only then UCR.
Controlled experiment. Replay a fixed production trace at fixed offered QPS against two configurations differing only in whether the deterministic cache is enabled. Hold model, weights, batch settings, and hardware topology constant.
Boundary conditions. On an 8-GPU single-node deployment with tensor parallelism, the cost is dominated by decode-step count, not by inter-GPU transfer; do not generalize this measurement to a multi-node deployment where collective communication would add a different term.
Numbers. No MEASURED cluster numbers are available in this review. All quantities above are the ones to measure, not results.
Rollback. If queue-delay improvement is within noise across three replay repetitions, close the cost-motivated workstream and re-justify the intervention on correctness grounds alone.
Scope. This is strictly a runtime/system capability measurement. It must not be reported as evidence about model domain capability.
risks: Trace replay at fixed QPS may not reproduce production burstiness, understating tail effects
Single-node conclusions do not transfer to multi-node collectives
Cost savings can be attributed to the intervention when they came from unrelated fleet changes
evidence_required: Fixed production trace and the replay harness configuration
KV-cache block-seconds and queue-delay distributions for both configurations, three repetitions
Hardware and parallelism topology record held constant across arms

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 177: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 6 - Training-data root cause: the redundancy was almost certainly synthesized into the SFT trajectories, so audit the data before touching the objective.
Mechanism. Trajectory generators that reward tool use produce corpora where nearly every turn contains a call. Supervised fine-tuning on that distribution makes 'call the tool' the maximum-likelihood continuation regardless of whether the answer is known. The behavior is then a faithful reproduction of the training prior, not a reasoning failure.
Falsifiable hypothesis H6. In the SFT corpus, the fraction of assistant turns containing a tool call exceeds the fraction in the target deployment distribution by a wide margin, and down-sampling no-call-needed items to match reduces UCR without any RL or preference stage.
Metrics. corpus call-rate by scenario family, deployment call-rate, UCR after data rebalancing, final correctness, and a check that no-tool items were not simply memorized.
Controlled experiment. Two fine-tunes from the identical base checkpoint, identical hyperparameters and seed, differing only in the mixture: original vs rebalanced with explicit no-call exemplars added. Evaluate on the same frozen eval set.
Boundary conditions. Loss masking must be verified first. If tool-call tokens and assistant tokens are masked inconsistently between the two runs, the comparison is void.
Numbers. No corpus statistics are MEASURED here. The claimed imbalance is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
Rollback. If the rebalanced run regresses tool_success_rate on items that genuinely require the tool by >2 absolute points, revert the mixture and escalate to a preference stage instead.
Scope. Data-provenance and training-mixture claim, provisional. Two fine-tunes on one seed cannot establish a capability improvement.
risks: Down-sampling tool-call items can induce under-calling on items that genuinely need the tool
Inconsistent loss masking between arms silently voids the comparison
Single-seed fine-tune comparisons are within run-to-run noise for small effects
evidence_required: Corpus call-rate histogram by scenario family versus deployment distribution
Loss-mask audit dump for both training runs on identical sample batches
Held-out tool-required subset accuracy for both arms

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 178: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 7 - Operational safety: the intervention is a behavior change to a deployed agent and must ship behind a staged, reversible rollout.
Mechanism of harm. Any abstention gate converts a class of tool calls into direct answers. Each converted call is a new opportunity to emit an unverified number. The failure mode is silent and confidently wrong, which is strictly worse operationally than a redundant call.
Falsifiable hypothesis H7. At a 1% traffic canary, the gated arm shows no increase in the confidently-wrong rate (wrong answer emitted with no tool evidence) relative to control, within a pre-registered non-inferiority margin.
Metrics. confidently-wrong rate (primary safety metric), UCR (efficiency metric, secondary), user-visible error rate, escalation/human-handoff rate, p95 latency.
Controlled experiment. Staged rollout 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, each stage held for a fixed observation window with a pre-declared automatic abort rule. Control arm runs concurrently, not historically.
Boundary conditions. Non-inferiority, not superiority, is the correct test for the safety metric; a superiority test would let a large efficiency win mask a small safety regression. Do not aggregate stages; each stage is evaluated on its own.
Numbers. The 1/5/25/100 ladder and the non-inferiority margin are ESTIMATEs set as policy before the experiment. They are not derived from any measurement in this corpus item.
Rollback. Automatic abort and full revert to control if the safety metric crosses the margin at any stage, if escalation rate rises, or if the observation window produces insufficient volume to decide.
Scope. Deployment-process claim. It governs how a change is validated and reverted; it makes no claim about model capability.
risks: Efficiency gains can mask a small but real safety regression if only superiority is tested
Historical controls instead of concurrent controls confound with traffic-mix drift
Insufficient canary volume yields an underpowered decision that looks like a pass
evidence_required: Per-stage canary dashboards with concurrent control arm
Pre-registered non-inferiority margin and abort rule, timestamped before rollout
Confidently-wrong incident samples with full trajectories

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 179: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 8 - Segment before aggregating: a single UCR number over mixed scenario families is uninterpretable.
Mechanism. 'The agent repeatedly calls a calculator' is a family of distinct behaviors: re-verification after a prior tool error, recomputation after a context truncation evicted the earlier result, echo-calling induced by a few-shot exemplar, and genuine ignorance of its own prior output. Each has a different fix, and an aggregate metric averages them into a number that no intervention can move predictably.
Falsifiable hypothesis H8. Redundant calls partition into these causes with an inter-annotator agreement of kappa >= 0.6, and at least one cause accounts for over half the volume. If the causes do not separate reliably, targeted intervention is unjustified and only the blunt deterministic cache is defensible.
Metrics. per-cause call counts, per-cause UCR, context-length at the moment of the redundant call (to test the truncation hypothesis), position of the redundant call within the trajectory.
Controlled experiment. Two independent annotators label 200 sampled redundant calls against a written codebook; compute kappa; then measure each candidate intervention only on its target segment.
Boundary conditions. The truncation cause is testable mechanically: if redundant calls cluster at context lengths near the window limit or near a summarization boundary, the fix is context management, not training.
Numbers. kappa >= 0.6 and N=200 are ESTIMATEs used as pre-registered acceptance bars. N=200 is chosen to give roughly +/-7 points of binomial resolution on a majority-share claim, which is stated so the reviewer can check the sample-size reasoning.
Rollback. If no cause exceeds half the volume, abandon targeted training work and keep only the cache.
Scope. Diagnostic framing, provisional. Segmentation results describe the logged system, not model competence.
risks: Annotator codebook drift produces spuriously high agreement on easy cases
Context-truncation cause can be confused with summarization-induced information loss
Optimizing one segment can shift volume into another rather than reducing total calls
evidence_required: Written annotation codebook and two independent label sets with kappa
Context-length distribution at the moment of each redundant call
Per-segment before/after call volumes for each intervention

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 180: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 9 - Reward design: if a preference stage is used, publish the scoring rule and adversarially probe it before any training compute is spent.
Mechanism. A reward that subtracts a per-call penalty from a correctness term has an exploitable degenerate optimum: never call, accept the correctness loss when the penalty coefficient is mis-set. The failure is not a training bug; it is the reward being wrong. It must be found by inspection and probing, not by watching loss curves.
Falsifiable hypothesis H9. Under the proposed reward, a hand-written always-abstain policy scores strictly lower than the current baseline policy on the same eval set. If it does not, the reward is degenerate and training must not start.
Metrics. reward of hand-written degenerate policies (always-abstain, always-call, call-once-then-answer) versus baseline; correlation between reward and human-judged trajectory quality on a held-out sample; reward variance across seeds.
Controlled experiment. Purely offline scoring of scripted policies. No GPU training required. This is the cheapest possible falsification and must precede any run.
Boundary conditions. Reward correlation with human judgment must be measured on trajectories not used to fit the reward. A reward validated only on its own training distribution proves nothing.
Numbers. No reward coefficients are proposed here as measured values. Any coefficient chosen later must be reported with the degenerate-policy scores that justified it.
Rollback. Do not start training until all three scripted degenerate policies score below baseline. If training starts and the policy's call rate collapses toward zero, halt at the first checkpoint and re-probe the reward rather than tuning the coefficient in flight.
Scope. Objective-design gate, provisional. Passing it authorizes a training attempt; it does not predict or demonstrate a capability gain.
risks: Penalty coefficient mis-set produces a policy that abstains on items requiring the tool
Reward validated on its own fitting distribution gives false assurance
In-flight coefficient tuning after a collapse contaminates the experimental record
evidence_required: Offline reward scores for always-abstain, always-call, and call-once scripted policies versus baseline
Held-out reward-vs-human-judgment correlation
Checkpoint-level call-rate trace during training

source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 181: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
STANCE 10 - Synthesis with an explicit spend ordering and a hard separation of system claims from model claims.
Ordering, cheapest falsification first. Step 1: build the counterfactual UCR estimator and validate the cheap proxy against it; without a defensible metric nothing downstream is interpretable. Step 2: ship the deterministic pre-tool cache in shadow, then serve; it removes the fleet cost with zero model risk. Step 3: segment redundant calls by cause and test the context-management fix, which is config-level and reversible. Step 4: audit the SFT mixture and loss masking. Step 5 only if steps 1-4 leave material harm: rebalance data, then a preference stage gated by the offline degenerate-policy probe. Step 6: staged canary with a non-inferiority safety test.
Falsifiable hypothesis H10. Steps 1-4, which require no weight updates, capture the majority of the achievable UCR reduction. If a weight update is required to move UCR at all, H10 is false and the extra training cost is justified; otherwise it is not.
Metrics carried through every step. counterfactual-UCR, tool_success_rate, final correctness, trajectory length in turns and tokens, p50/p95 tool and end-to-end latency, recovery rate after injected tool failure, confidently-wrong rate.
Confounders to control globally. Frozen eval set with item-level provenance, concurrent rather than historical controls, seeds recorded, and no eval-set edits between arms.
Numbers. Every threshold named across these stances is an ESTIMATE functioning as a pre-registration value. This review contains no MEASURED result.
Rollback gates. Each step has its own revert path: cache disabled by config flag, context-management change reverted by config, data/mixture change reverted by checkpoint rollback, canary aborted by the non-inferiority rule.
Scope. Any improvement demonstrated by steps 1-4 is a runtime/system result about the scaffold and serving path. Only step 5, with multiple seeds and an independent benchmark, could support a claim about model domain capability, and it would still be provisional.
risks: Treating a scaffold-level UCR win as evidence of improved model capability
Eval-set edits between steps silently break cross-step comparability
Cumulative small regressions across six steps with no end-to-end re-baseline
evidence_required: Step-by-step decision log recording which hypothesis passed or failed and what was spent
Frozen eval set with item-level provenance hashes
End-to-end re-baseline after the final step, compared against the original baseline
